hints: Let $X$ be the number of people who agree to complete the survey out of 3. Model $X$ as $X \sim \mathrm{B}(3, 0.2)$.
The event at least one completes is the complement of no one completes: $\mathrm{P}(X \ge 1) = 1 - \mathrm{P}(X = 0)$.
Calculate $\mathrm{P}(X = 0) = (1 - 0.2)^3 = (0.8)^3$ and subtract the result from 1.
walkthrough:
Identify the complement event for at least one person agreeing:
$$\mathrm{P}(\text{at least 1 agrees}) = 1 - \mathrm{P}(\text{none agree})$$

Calculate the probability that all 3 people decline, where each person declines with probability $1 - 0.2 = 0.8$:
$$\mathrm{P}(\text{none agree}) = (0.8)^3 = 0.512$$

Subtract from 1 to obtain the required probability:
$$\mathrm{P}(\text{at least 1 agrees}) = 1 - 0.512 = 0.488 = \frac{61}{125}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Method 1: Using complementary probability
Step 1: Define the random variable.
Let $X$ represent the number of people who agree to complete the survey out of the first $3$ people asked.
Since people are chosen randomly and independently with constant probability $p = 0.2$, $X \sim \mathrm{B}(3, 0.2)$ with failure probability $q = 1 - 0.2 = 0.8$.

Step 2: Formulate the complement event.
The phrase at least one means $X \ge 1$, which includes $X = 1, 2, 3$.
The only outcome not included is $X = 0$ (all three decline):
$$\mathrm{P}(X \ge 1) = 1 - \mathrm{P}(X = 0)$$

Step 3: Evaluate $\mathrm{P}(X = 0)$:
$$\mathrm{P}(X = 0) = (0.8)^3 = 0.512$$

Step 4: Subtract from $1$:
$$\mathrm{P}(X \ge 1) = 1 - 0.512 = 0.488 = \frac{61}{125}$$

Method 2: Direct sum of binomial probabilities
Sum the mutually exclusive probabilities for $1, 2,$ and $3$ people agreeing:
$$\mathrm{P}(X = 1) = \binom{3}{1} (0.2)^1 (0.8)^2 = 3 \times 0.2 \times 0.64 = 0.384$$
$$\mathrm{P}(X = 2) = \binom{3}{2} (0.2)^2 (0.8)^1 = 3 \times 0.04 \times 0.8 = 0.096$$
$$\mathrm{P}(X = 3) = \binom{3}{3} (0.2)^3 (0.8)^0 = 1 \times 0.008 \times 1 = 0.008$$
$$\text{Total} = 0.384 + 0.096 + 0.008 = 0.488 = \frac{61}{125}$$
